- **R2-2's per-kind truncation is correct through the whole path.** `search()` calls
  `capped(filtered(all), to:)`, so the scope filter runs BEFORE the count and each kind's `over` is
  about rows that survived scoping; `listBody` reads `listingIsTruncated` (it draws every kind) and
  `notesBody` reads `notesAreTruncated` (it draws `hits.filter { $0.kind == .post }`). I re-derived
  the 41-books/3-notes case by hand and ran the pin.
- **The cap lift is bounded by the answer, not the corpus.** With a day armed `limitPerKind` is nil,
  and both the books and blocks arms are skipped (`ShelfQueries.swift:434` and `:479` guard on
  `editedOn == nil`), so nothing unbounded reads a second kind; the post arm's `LIMIT -1` is SQLite's
  own "no limit". The derived reads (`loadTagChips`, `loadNoteCards`, the eager `DisplayTitle.note`
  map) run over the day's answer, and both docs now say so with the ceiling named. Cost ∝ the
  answer, never ∝ the corpus — R2-3's landing is honest.

  zero-width stamp contributes `tail = 0`, adds no gap to either branch, leaves `baseline` and both

#### THE MOUNT-ORDERING TRACE (written BEFORE the code, as the brief requires)

**The question:** at a mount, which arrives first — the FIRST honest geometry report (which decides
the restore) or the projection that arms the landing (`TakesChoreographer.consumeLandings` →
`landArticle`)?

**The answer is: IT DEPENDS ON THE SURFACE, and both orders are real — so the condition needs both
halves the brief anticipated.** Traced by reading, three facts:

1. **In the APP the GEOMETRY is first.** `TakesBoardView`'s article `ScrollView` exists from the very
   first layout pass whether or not the note has slots — `singleColumnArticle`
   (`TakesBoardView.swift:554–575`) renders `TakesEmptyStateView` INSIDE the `ScrollView` when
   `model.projection.slots.isEmpty`. So `onScrollGeometryChange` (`:646`) fires with `viewport > 0`
   on that first pass. The projection, by contrast, arrives from `.task { await model.start() }`
   (`:176`) → `observeTakes` → `deliver` → `adopt` (`TakesViewModel.swift:418`), which is
   asynchronous and therefore lands AFTER the first layout. `consumeLandings` (`:456`) — and with it
   the only two `landArticle` callers in the codebase (the bloom arm and the N9 entry arm,
   `TakesChoreographer.swift:167–186` / `:189–212`) — runs inside `adopt`. **So on the real board the
   restore has already entered `.wanted(remembered)` by the time the landing is armed.**
2. **…and the restore cannot have MOVED anything yet.** Before `adopt` the article has zero rows, so
   the restore's `.scrollToRow(rowID)` is a proxy scroll at an id the column does not hold — a no-op
   (the same fact R1-4 rests on). That is what makes the second half of the condition sufficient:
   settling the restore at `landArticle` time cancels it before it can scroll for real.
3. **In the PIN HARNESS the LANDING is first.** `TakesArticleScrollTests.landingModel` calls
   `adopt` BEFORE `mount` (`:180–190`), exactly as `CommandRoutingTests` does, so the landing is
   already armed when the first geometry report arrives and the restore is still `.undecided`.

**Consequence for the condition's home — both halves, one rule.** A single pure predicate
(`TakesBoardLayout.landingOutranks(_:remembered:)`) is consulted at the two places the two orders
reach:
  **(i)** `consumeArticleGeometry`'s `.undecided` branch — a landing already pending that names a row
  OTHER than the remembered one settles the restore at once, no scroll issued (the harness's order,
  and the app's if a projection ever lands before the first geometry);
  **(ii)** `landArticle(on:)` — a restore already `.wanted(place)` whose `place.rowID` differs from
  the arriving landing is settled on the spot (the app's order).
A `.settled` restore is left alone in both (nothing to cancel), and a memory of `.top` already
settles at once with no scroll, so a landing trivially wins there and no branch is owed.

#### PIECE 3 — R3-1: THE PICK LEAVES IN THE SAME UPDATE THE MODE DOES (and R3-6 rides it)

**The mechanism, traced myself before the fix.** R2-1's own fix made `modeChanged()` `async` so it
could fold in the re-read, and the whole handler became
`.onChange(of: model.mode) { _, _ in Task { await model.modeChanged() } }`. A `Task {}` body cannot
run before the current synchronous update completes, so `clearSelection()` — the FIRST statement
inside that function — was deferred off the very update in which the mode changed. Neither consumer
of the selection is mode-gated: the bulk bar is `if selectedPosts.count > 1` inside the header's
control row, which every mode draws, and it carries
`Button("Delete \(selectedPosts.count) notes…", role: .destructive)`; the info panel hangs off
`model.infoHit` in the same window. So with two or more notes picked in List, switching to Notes or
Timeline rendered at least one frame of a destructive door over a selection nothing on screen shows —
which is what `clearSelection`'s own doc calls the invisible-selection hazard, and what P-0's rule in
the `.onChange`'s own comment forbids.

**The fix, the reviewer's own shape:** `func modeChanged() -> Bool` — clear synchronously, return
whether a day was cleared — and `.onChange { if model.modeChanged() { Task { await model.search() } } }`.
The model's convention (write here, the caller spawns the read) therefore **stops bending**: R2-1's
doc said it "bends exactly once, here, because the caller is an `onChange` that cannot know whether
anything was cleared", and the answer is simply to tell it. That sentence is replaced with this one
in the code.

**R3-6 rides the same function:** `modeChanged` wrote `editedOn = nil` directly, past the door the
field's `private(set)` exists to force; it now calls `setEditedOn(nil)`. Byte-identical behaviour
today (nil takes the same path) — the point is that two writers of one field is how a future clause
inside that door (QUESTIONS #104's option (c), say) gets skipped on one of the two roads.

**RED ON OLD — MEASURED BY BEHAVIORAL REVERT, then RESTORED** (announced in the previous commit
before it started; pre-revert copies in `scratchpad/17q-prerevert/`, restored with `git checkout --`
and verified byte-identical by `diff`; **no revert is in flight**). This one is a COMPILE red by its
nature and the reviewer said so: on the pre-fix tree `modeChanged()` was `async`, so there is no way
to read the selection in the same turn that changed the mode — the pin cannot be written. With the
model's signature back to `async` and the view's `onChange` back to `Task { await … }`
(`/tmp/17q-red3b.log`, local):

```
LibraryDayFilterTests.swift:337:31: error: binary operator '==' cannot be applied to operands of type '()' and 'Bool'
LibraryDayFilterTests.swift:365:41: error: binary operator '==' cannot be applied to operands of type '()' and 'Bool'
LibraryDayFilterTests.swift:405:22: error: cannot convert value of type '()' to expected condition type 'Bool'
```

…and with only the MODEL reverted, the view's own call site fails first
(`LibraryCatalogView.swift:225:22: error: cannot convert value of type '()' to expected condition
type 'Bool'`, `/tmp/17q-red3.log`) — which is the fix stated as a type: the door's shape is what
makes the caller able to clear now and read later. Restored and green again.

**Pins.** `LibraryDayFilterTests.theModeChangeClearsThePickInItsOwnUpdate` (new) — two notes picked
and an info subject set, the mode flipped, `modeChanged()` called with **no `await` between it and
the assertion**, the pick and the info subject both gone, and the returned answer `false` (no day, no
re-read owed); then with a day armed the answer flips to `true` and the day is gone. The two shipped
pins that drove the old door are updated to drive the new one, and each gained an assertion rather
than losing one: `leavingTheCatalogClearsTheDay` now also states that the Notes mode owes NO re-read
and the Timeline does; `returningToTheCatalogListsTheWholeLibraryAgain` drives exactly what the view
does (`if model.modeChanged() { await model.search() }`). **The frame itself is not reachable from a
headless pin** — the rig cannot mount the whole catalog (KnownIssues) — so the walk carries the face.

**What the walk changed in my understanding — ONE OBSERVATION FOR HER, recorded rather than
re-decided.** The brief anticipated it in words (*"a landing that names a block INSIDE the remembered
page but not at its top still wins under her letter"*); the walk measured how WIDE that is. Because
the memory is **the row at the top of the page** and the landing is **the block she came from**, the
two are equal only when her current block happens to be the row at the fold — which a hand scroll
almost never produces. So **with an entry landing present, the restore in practice never runs**, and
what she gets is: her block always on screen, one move, and a stable page (every round trip measured
pixel-identical). What she loses is the surrounding context she had scrolled to when her block was
already visible but not at the top (`04` → `05`). That is her letter, built to the brief's own
definition of "the same block", and the alternative reading — *"the same block" means the note's
current block did not CHANGE while she was away*, which would make every plain round trip restore
exactly and only a deliberate click elsewhere win — is a small addition, not one line: it needs a
second session value (which block was current when the board was last shown) beside
`takesArticlePlaces`. **Hers to say; nothing here re-opens R-Q20.**

**→ RULED R-Q21 (her evening sitting, 2026-09-12, on the orchestrator's J14): the alternative
reading. BUILT AT PIECE 6**, with the second session value exactly as named above — and with one
thing this observation did not foresee, which the piece's own walk found: re-keying the predicate is
not enough, the landing has to STAND DOWN on a plain round trip or it races the restore through the
lazy column's settling passes. See piece 6.**

#### PIECE 6 — R-Q21: "THE SAME BLOCK" IS THE CURRENT BLOCK, NOT THE REMEMBERED ROW

**Her ruling (§7, R-Q21, on J14):** *"the same block"* means the note's CURRENT block did not CHANGE
while she was away — a plain round trip restores the page exactly as she left it; the landing wins
only when she comes back on a DIFFERENT block than the one she was in when she left Takes. This
replaces the brief's own definition (the landing's row equals the remembered top row), which I built
at piece 1 and then MEASURED at the walk: the two coincide only when her block straddles the fold, so
the restore practically never ran and a plain mode switch moved the page — the thing her own reason
for R-Q20 argues against.

**What shipped — one new session value, the same ONE predicate, the same TWO consult sites.**

1. **`EditorRouter.takesArticleCurrentRows[postID]`** — the `placementID` of the block current on the
   Takes board, `@ObservationIgnored`, session-only, riding beside `takesArticlePlaces` because the
   two answer one question together (where the page was, and which block she was in there). A
   PLACEMENT id and not a block id, so the comparison against a landing — which IS a placement id —
   needs no map at the moment it is made.
2. **`TakesBoardLayout.articleLastCurrentRow`** — a `let`, snapshotted from that store in
   `TakesViewModel.init` and **never moved after**. It has to be a per-mount CONSTANT: the value is a
   fact about the PREVIOUS showing, and this mount overwrites the session's copy within milliseconds
   (`consumeLandings` sets the entry ring — which writes it — BEFORE it sets the landing), so a live
   read would compare the landing against itself and the memory would always win. The session's copy
   is the NEXT mount's snapshot; the layout's is this mount's question. *(That ordering is the one
   real trap in this piece, and it is written at the property.)*
3. **`landingOutranks(_:lastCurrentRow:)`** — re-keyed, still ONE pure predicate, still consulted at
   `consumeArticleGeometry`'s `.undecided` branch and at `landArticle(on:)`. The two nil cases are
   stated in its doc and pinned: **no landing ⇒ the memory rules** (unchanged); **a landing with no
   recorded prior current block ⇒ the landing rules** — we cannot claim "the same block" about a
   showing we have no record of, and the case is either a first entry (no memory to restore, so it
   costs nothing) or a mount that went away before its projection landed.
4. **Two write sites, both on the view model, both gated on `landingEnabled`** (as the place already
   is, so the Write panel's embedded model never writes here): `landAuthorityFocus` (the entry ring)
   and `focus`'s `.migrated` arm (a click that moves the ring). **Deliberately NOT the geometry
   hook** — a click that moves the ring without scrolling must still count, or leaving right after it
   would read as "she moved blocks while away" when she moved them while here. **`TakesChoreographer`
   is untouched**, as the brief fences.

**RED ON THE AS-BUILT RULE, measured by behavioral revert and restored** (`75d690ff`'s predicate and
its two call sites put back; pre-revert copy in `scratchpad/17q-p6-prerevert/`; **no revert is in

**R1-1 · MAJOR · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Takes/TakesBoardLayout.swift:788–800` (`articlePlaceNow`) + `:886–889` (`restoreStep`'s settle: `abs(frame.minY) <= 2`) + `:716–723` (`ArticlePlace`, "the sub-row place is deliberately not promised") · THE OPEN ROW'S REAL MECHANISM — R-Q21's *"exactly as she left it"* is delivered at ROW precision only, and the record points the fix pass at the wrong seam.** *Mechanism, traced then measured:* the memory is the row STRADDLING the fold (`articlePlaceNow`: "the lowest row whose top is at or above the fold"), and the restore aligns that row's TOP to the fold. So a page whose top row straddled the fold by `s` pt comes back `s` pt lower (content shifted down by `s`), and everything below it — the block she was in — moves toward the page's bottom edge by exactly `s`. On the 46-pt-row fixture `s` is at most a row; on *A Scandal in Bohemia* a straddling paragraph is one to three hundred points, which is enough to carry a block that sat "mid-page with four blocks below it" to the edge — the walk's `17` → `18`. The second round trip is pixel-identical because the first one left the top row aligned (`s == 0`), and a small re-scroll that keeps the same top row lands on the same settled frame — both of the walk's "deterministic" observations fall out of this. **Measured (probe 2, the record's own road: the entry ring on block 41 of 60, her scroll, leave, return with nothing clicked):** the top row is the SAME on both mounts (`sameTopAsA=true`); her block sat 571 pt below the fold on mount A (`(212, 1776, 676, 46)` against visible `1205…1824` — on screen at the edge) and 618 pt below it on mount B (`(212, 1622, 676, 46)` against `1004…1623` — one point visible): a 47-pt shift, one row's straddle, with `landing=nil`, `restore=settled`, `restoreAims=3`. **What the record blames is ruled out by the same probe:** the window's first responder IS her pane (`frIsHerPane=true`, `live=true`) and the pane sits OFF-SCREEN — AppKit did not scroll it into view; and Apple documents no scroll on `makeFirstResponder`, `becomeFirstResponder`, `setSelectedRange(_:)` or `setSelectedRanges(_:affinity:stillSelecting:)` (the `stillSelecting` clause governs notifications and marked text only; `ScrollPosition.isPositionedByUser` is documented only as "whether the scroll view has been positioned by the user" — nothing on AppKit-originated scrolls). The `PaneSurface` seam the record names (`:1289–1300`, the caret + `makeFirstResponder`) is therefore the wrong discriminator, and a change there would be the guess pin-before-fix forbids. *Fix:* sub-row precision in the memory, on the restore's own principle (absolute, idempotent, settled when the ROW says so): remember the first row whose top is at or BELOW the fold together with its `into` (0…viewport), and restore it by `column.scrollTo(row, anchor: UnitPoint(x: 0, y: into / (viewportHeight - rowHeight)))` — a well-formed unit point for any row shorter than the viewport (a taller row falls back to `.top`, today's rule), settled when the row's `minY ≈ into`; the TOP place (R1-1 of 17p) and the ONE proxy scroll mechanism unchanged; the `(id, anchor)` binding is what SwiftUI re-applies on relayout (J1(c)), which is why an anchor beats a relative nudge (J2's doubling). The record's own three mounted pins pass PRECISELY because they assert `abs(isAt - wasAt) <= 1` — the granularity that hides this.

### 17q LADDER — ROUND 1 · THE IMPLEMENTER'S RESPONSES

*The 17q implementer (`opus-implementer`) under the cross-model flow: agree/dispute traced against the
code at `42536eae` in my own context — nothing implemented, no code or test file touched, no suite
run; this plan is the only file this edits. **8 AGREED · 0 DISPUTED**, six of them with a rider the
reviewer's fix sketch would otherwise get wrong. The reviewer makes the final call on each and
implements its confirmed fixes itself.*

**R1-1 (MAJOR — the open row's real mechanism is the restore's ROW precision, not the pane seam) —
AGREE on the mechanism and the fix, AGREE that my diagnosis was unsupported, and ONE RIDER THAT
MATTERS: the walk's own numbers are bigger than one straddle, and the reviewer's probe says so too.**

Re-read and confirmed: `articlePlaceNow` keeps the row with the LARGEST `minY` among those `<= 0.5` —
the row straddling the fold, at `minY == -s` — and `restoreStep` aims `anchor: .top` and settles at
`abs(minY) <= 2`, i.e. at `minY == 0`. So the restored page sits `s` pt lower in the content and
every row below the fold, her block included, is `s` pt further down. That is a real defect, it is
mine, and the fix's shape (sub-row precision as an ANCHOR on the absolute, idempotent, row-settled
restore, with `.top` kept for a row taller than the viewport and the ONE proxy as the scroll) is the
right one. **I also accept that my `PaneSurface` diagnosis is not supported:** the probe measured the
first responder to BE her pane with the pane off screen — AppKit did not scroll it — which is a
direct measurement of the thing I could only hypothesise, and my record said so in those words ("what
it points AT", "the discriminator is named"). It was an untested hypothesis and the reviewer tested
it. **What I hold that the reviewer does not: the two walk captures.** Reading `17` and `18` (the
262-block note, her block 98 mid-page, ⌘1/⌘2): the page's TOP ROW CHANGED — *"Holmes laughed."* in
`17`, *"Stolen, then."* in `18` — with four rows now standing above where one row stood, and her
block's card moved down by ≈295 pt (≈342 px at the capture's displayed scale). The reviewer's probe
reports the opposite for its own case (`sameTopAsA=true`, a 47-pt shift). **Both can be true — one
straddle is bounded by the straddling row's height and that fixture's rows are 46 pt — but a
295-pt shift with the top row four rows earlier is NOT accounted for by a one-row straddle on a page
whose visible top row was a single line.** So: the fix is right and owed; it may not be the whole of
the open row. **The rider, concretely: the fix pass must RE-WALK frames `17`/`18` on the real
262-block note and compare, not close the row on the probe** — the probe's fixture cannot produce the
magnitude the walk shows, and "the pins pass at the granularity that hides this" is exactly the trap
the reviewer names, one level up. A second contributor I could not rule out and flag rather than
assert: the memory is written from EVERY `.settled` geometry report, so a report arriving during the
board's teardown (the content shrinking as rows leave) would record a place she never saw — that is a
read, not a measurement, and it is the next thing I would instrument.

**R1-2 (MAJOR — the stand-down clears the fan-panel BLOOM landing too) — AGREE, it is mine, and the
self-contradiction the reviewer found is mine twice over.**

Confirmed at the sites: `consumeLandings`' bloom arm (`TakesChoreographer.swift:171–181`) runs
`board.bloom` → `model.focus(…)` → `board.landArticle(on: slot.placementID)`, and my
`resolveLandingAgainstAPendingRestore` compares that placement against `articleLastCurrentRow` with

8's door stops going there. And the reviewer is right that her rulings do not reach it: R-Q20 names
*"the entry landing"* and R-Q21 names *"a plain round trip … nothing clicked"*; a fan-panel door is a
click. **The contradiction is worse than a stale paragraph:** `landingOutranks`'s last paragraph
(which I wrote at piece 6's first half) says standing the landing down "would also stand down the
fan-panel bloom door's *'go there'* … it is not this piece's" — and then the walk made me build
exactly that in the second half, and I did not go back and re-read my own reason for not doing it.
That is the finding. **Riders for the fix, two:** (1) **it needs one token in
`TakesChoreographer`**, at `:180` and `:204` — the brief's *"`TakesChoreographer` still untouched"*
was the ORCHESTRATOR's scope fence for piece 6, not a canon rule, and this is precisely the change
that earns lifting it; say so rather than working around it (a `kind:` parameter defaulted to
`.entry` keeps all twenty-two test call sites compiling unmodified). (2) **the distinction must land
at BOTH stand-down sites** — the resolver AND the `.undecided` branch's inline copy (R1-3) — or the

**R1-3 (MINOR, F-0 — the layout at 1,017 lines; the stand-down written twice) — AGREE, and the
mechanical fold is NOT mechanical: here is the line the sketch would get wrong.**

Confirmed: the `.undecided` branch spells the rule itself (`!landingOutranks(…)` inside the guard,
then `articleLanding = nil` after entering `.wanted`) instead of calling the one resolver, so my
record's *"ONE private method, consulted from the same two sites"* is not literally true — it is one
PREDICATE at two sites and one METHOD at one of them. **The rider:** the guard does two jobs at once
— it decides whether to enter `.wanted` AND what to RETURN. Folding it as sketched ("enter `.wanted`
and call the resolver") changes the return: after the resolver settles a restore that should not run,
the branch must return `rememberStep(geometry)`, not `restoreStep(…)`, or it issues the very scroll
her ruling removes. The fold therefore needs a re-check of `articleRestore` after the resolver call,
and the pure pin's arm (a) — `.remember(.top)` with `articleRestoreAims == 0` — is what catches it if
it is got wrong. On the split: I agree `TakesArticleScroll` is the right home and that 17q made the
row worse (610 of 1,017 lines), and I would not do the split inside a ladder fix pass — the 17p
ladder's own R1-6 took that position and the orchestrator sustained it.

**R1-4 (MINOR — the words oracle grows; the doc claims a teardown that does not exist) — AGREE; the
sentence is mine and it is false.**

Confirmed by grep: `CatalogStampOracle.reset(_:)` has no production caller, only the four pins;
`catalogStampFlipDoor` tears down `flip[postID]` and nothing tears down `shown[postID]`. My doc
claimed R2-9's hygiene was "applied at birth" and it was applied to half of it. **Rider:** clearing
the slot from `recordCatalogStamp`'s own `onDisappear` is the right shape and is better than a
card-level `reset(postID)` — the modifier sits on the `Text` inside `if let words`, so a stamp that
stops being drawn (the `ViewThatFits` arrangement swapping, or the List row's day slot standing down
under the `date` sort) clears exactly its own slot and leaves the others. No pin breaks: all four pins
`reset` before mounting, and none asserts a slot's presence across a disappearance.

**R1-5 (NIT — R3-10's half: the new note's flip door is never registered on a `.task(id:)` swap) —
AGREE, it is the half-step my own fix left.**

Confirmed: `.onAppear` registers `flipStamp[postID]` once, my `onChange(of: postID)` now clears the
OLD note's entries, and on a swap where the view is reused `onAppear` does not re-fire — so the new
note has no flip door until a remount. Before 17q the stale old entry survived; now neither exists.
**Rider on the sketch:** register in the `.task(id: postID)` body that already resets `showsCreated`
and `stamps`, rather than in `onChange` — `task(id:)` runs on a fresh mount AND on every swap, so one
site covers both roads with no double-registration, and its first statements are synchronous (before
`await watch()`), so it is as prompt as `onAppear`. Registering in `onChange` alone would leave a
fresh mount without a door.

**R1-6 (NIT — the two renderers state different FACTS for a no-stated-day note under `date`) —
AGREE, and the clause needs to say what the row's options actually are.**

Confirmed: the card's one rule fills the second slot with the edit stamp (my recorded call (iii)) and
the List row shows nothing — `listDay` is nil because `sortIsTheStatedDay`, and the trailing
`rowStamp(.entryDate)` is nil because she stated no day. I recorded (iii) as a CARD consequence and
the reviewer is right that the row's silence is its other half. **Rider the clause must carry:** the
row cannot simply be given the edit stamp. Its trailing stamp is fenced by the brief (*"no change to
the List row's TRAILING stamp"*), so the only lever is `listDay` — and under the `date` sort
`listDay` must stay nil or the row prints one day twice, which is R3-2, the thing this entry fixed.
Making the row match the card is therefore a change to the FENCED slot, i.e. hers, and the clause
should say so rather than reading as a one-line tidy.

**R1-7 (NIT — `rowStamp` computed three times per row) — AGREE, and the substitution is already
pinned, so no new pin is owed.**

Confirmed at `postRow`: `rowStamps(...)` (which calls `rowStamp` twice) for `date:` and a third
`rowStamp(...)` for `stamp:`. **Rider:** `pair.sorted` is byte-identical to `rowStamp(sort, for:
hit)` under every sort by the type's own definition (`sortIsTheStatedDay ? stated : other`, and
`stated == rowStamp(.entryDate)` exactly when that is the sort), and the pure pin already asserts
both halves (`pair.other == LibrarySortFace.rowStamp(sort, for: hit)` and `dated.sorted ==
dated.stated`) — so the substitution is covered by existing assertions and
`LibrarySortMenuTests.aRowsStampIsTheSortsOwnStampInWords`, which drives `rowStamp` directly, rides
unmodified.

**R1-8 (NIT — the small card's flip is not reset on a sort change) — AGREE, with a correction to the
reset's KEY.**

Confirmed: `showsTheOther` is `@State` on `CatalogCardStamps` with no `.id`, so a sort change
re-renders the same identity and the flip survives — showing a different fact without a click.
**Rider:** the sketch's key (`stamps.sortIsTheStatedDay`) is too narrow. Switching `edited` →
`created` leaves that flag false while `other`'s SUBJECT changes from edited to created, so the
flipped card silently swaps facts and the reset never fires. The honest key is the fact's identity —
`stamps.sorted.subject` — not the flag and not the whole `stamps` value (which changes whenever a
note's edit stamp merely moves, and a glance gesture should not be cancelled by an autosave). That
matches the masthead's rule, whose reset is per NOTE and not per keystroke.

fraction, so the row's top lands at `a·(viewport − rowHeight)`; setting that to `into` gives
`a = into / (viewport − rowHeight)` — which is what `ArticlePlace.anchorY` computes, with the clamp

behaviour. Both 17p measurements still hold and the doc still carries them: the identity is the ROW

24-aim bound with the page close but not exact. That is the bound doing its job; it is worth nobody's
code, only this sentence.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**R2-1 · MAJOR · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Takes/TakesBoardLayout.swift:368` (`landArticle`: `if case .wanted = articleRestore { resolveEntryLandingAgainstTheMemory() }`) + `:944` (the `.undecided` branch's resolver call) + `:372–402` (the resolver's doc, "the TOP included") · THE `.top` STAND-DOWN IS BUILT IN ONE MOUNT ORDER ONLY — in the APP's order a page left AT REST comes back with her block revealed at the foot on a plain round trip, which is R-Q21's letter falsified on the very shape the round-1 fix pass, the sanity pass (its note (3)) and the dispositions all recorded as delivered.** *Mechanism, traced:* a `.top` memory never reaches `.wanted` — the `.undecided` branch settles it at once (`:947–950`); in the app the entry landing arrives AFTER that first geometry (the projection lands on the view's `.task`), and `landArticle` consults the resolver only `if case .wanted`, so an entry landing on the block she was in is never weighed, lives, and reveals. In the HARNESS order (the landing pending at the first geometry) the `.undecided` branch's resolver stands it down — the only order `aBloomLandingRidesThroughTheRestoreInBothOrders`'s arm `t` (`TakesArticleScrollTests.swift:1620`) pins. *Measured, pure (probe 1):* `freshBoard(lastCurrentRow: "was-here")` · `consumeArticleGeometry(offset 0, remembered: .top, order: nil)` → `.remember(.top)`, `.settled` · `landArticle(on: "was-here")` → **`articleLanding == "was-here"`** (the harness order beside it: `nil`). *Measured, USE (captures `39` → `40`):* A Scandal in Bohemia entered on block 238 (revealed at the foot, `34`); single-line wheel steps UP to rest (`39`: "I." under the top padding — the page at rest); ⌘1 · ⌘2 → **the page is `34` again, byte-identical (`cmp`)**: block 238 revealed at the foot — the "keeps trying to jump to the bottom" class on a plain round trip. *Fix:* the layout records, per mount, whether a memory was READ at the first geometry (`articleMemoryAtMount = remembered`, set in the `.undecided` branch before the resolver); `landArticle` consults the resolver whenever `articleRestore != .undecided && articleMemoryAtMount != nil` — a `.wanted` restore is one such case, a `.top` memory settled at once is the other; the first entry (no memory ⇒ nothing to come back to) and a bloom (the kind guard) are unchanged; **R2-1 (MAJOR — the `.top` stand-down is built in the harness's order only) — AGREE; confirmed by

Re-read at the two sites and it is exactly as traced: a `.top` memory never reaches `.wanted` — the

**Rider 1 — the new condition is right, and I checked the road that would have made it wrong.** In
the HARNESS order `landArticle` fires before any geometry, so `articleRestore == .undecided` and the
memory has not been read; `articleRestore != .undecided && articleMemoryAtMount != nil` is false
there and the `.undecided` branch still does the work — unchanged, and the pins that ride that order
keep asserting the same thing. **Rider 2 — a BLOOM must not start standing down on a `.top` memory,
and it does not:** the resolver's first guard is `articleLanding != nil, articleLandingKind == .entry`

the 17p arm did at the fix pass:** `theLandingOutranksAMoveToAnotherBlockButNotAPlainRoundTrip`'s arm
(f) is commented *"The TOP remembered already settles at once and issues no scroll (R1-1), so a

was not consulted for `.top`, and after this fix it is true only for a landing that OUTRANKS. Its
assertions still hold (arm (f)'s landing is `"far"` against `lastCurrentRow` `"was-here"`), so the pin
rides; the comment must not.

**R2-2 (MAJOR — W-2's re-derivation has no departure half) — AGREE, and the rider is the one hazard I
raised at round 1 for the wrong finding: it is live HERE, and the sketch as written would trip it.**

The mechanism reads exactly as traced: `articlePlaceNow` takes the LOWEST-`minY` fitting frame, a
de-realized row's last frame stays in `articleRowFrames` until `forgetArticleRowFrame`, and the
forget removes it without re-deriving — so a stale small `minY` wins every comparison while it is
present and nothing recomputes when it goes. That is the asymmetry, and W-2's own doc names the case
it leaves open ("a fling's last step is pages").

**THE RIDER — the departure re-derivation must not fire while the board is TEARING DOWN.** I hold the
write sites: `TakesBoardView`'s rows carry `.onDisappear { model.rowDisappeared(…);
model.forgetArticleRowFrame(slot.placementID) }`, and SwiftUI runs those `onDisappear`s when the
BOARD's subtree is removed — every row, one after another, on a mode switch. With the sketch as
written each of those departures would re-derive and WRITE the session memory from a shrinking set of
frames, so the last row to leave decides what she comes back to. That is the hazard I named in my
round-1 rider as "a report arriving during the board's teardown would record a place she never saw" —
the reviewer was right that it was not R1-1's mechanism, and it becomes real the moment the departure
writes. **Two candidate guards, and it must be MEASURED either way** (a mounted pin: mount, scroll to
a known place, tear the board down, then assert `takesArticlePlaces[post]` still equals the place the
last settled geometry wrote — red if the unmount overwrote it): (a) re-derive on departure only while
frames REMAIN that could name a place — but note a one-by-one unmount still walks down to one row, so
a bare `!articleRowFrames.isEmpty` is not enough; (b) suppress memory writes once the board is
leaving, which needs a fact the layout can see (`TakesViewModel.teardown()` sets it; the board view
calls that in its own `.onDisappear`, whose ordering against the rows' is not guaranteed — so the
flag must be set where it is certainly first, or the guard must be (a)-shaped). I have no preference
between them; I have the requirement that the pin exist before the departure half ships.

**R2-3 (MAJOR — R1-1's shift survives where no row below the fold fits) — AGREE on the mechanism, and
the gate is right — but the finding's two shapes are NOT one problem, and half of it needs no
measurement at all.**

The `fits` test is `into + rowHeight <= viewport`, i.e. exactly "the anchor's unit point lies in
[0, 1]", so the fallback is 17p's rule kept for the shapes the anchor cannot express — that much is
right. **The split, from the arithmetic I re-derived at the sanity pass:** the anchor puts a row's top
at `a·(viewport − rowHeight)` = `a·room`.

- **A TALL row (`rowHeight > viewport`, so `room < 0`) straddling the fold (`into < 0`)** — the
  bloomed fan, a paragraph taller than the page, the case the finding names second — gives
  `a = into/room` = negative ÷ negative = **POSITIVE, and ≤ 1 whenever the row covers the bottom
  edge** (`into >= room` ⇔ `maxY >= viewport`). So that half is expressible with an ordinary
  in-range unit point TODAY and needs no `scrollTo` measurement; what blocks it is
  `ArticlePlace.anchorY`'s guard `room > 1, into > 0` (`:814–816`), which rejects every negative room
  and every negative `into` alike. Splitting that guard is the fix for the tall half.
- **A SHORT row straddling (`room > 0`, `into < 0`)** — the short-note case the captures measure
  (`32` → `33`, ~9 pt) — is the one that needs `a < 0`, and that is the measurement the finding
  gates on. Its gate is right and I would not skip it.

**Rider 2 — a THIRD zero-`into` branch the finding does not name:** `articlePlaceNow`'s last fallback
is `below` (`:904`), also constructed with `into 0`. It is reached when no row fits and none straddles
— every realized row at or below the fold and the topmost not fitting. For a TALL row with `into > 0`
that fallback is correct by impossibility (a unit point cannot put a tall row's top below the fold at
all), and saying so in the doc is worth more than code; for a short row extending past the bottom edge
it is the same shift in a third place, rare but real. Whichever way the measurement goes, the doc
should name all three branches rather than the straddling one.

**R2-4 (NIT — the pin's doc conflates two orders) — AGREE.** The doc is the fix pass's, not mine, and
the distinction is the one my own mount-ordering trace turned on: `.onAppear` vs the first geometry is

**R2-5 (NIT — the dead branch) — AGREE.** `UnitPoint.top` is `UnitPoint(x: 0.5, y: 0)`, so

#### R-5 · THE RECEIPT-SITE CLASSIFICATION (every site that reaches `StatusCenter`, with its verdict)

**The rule I classified by**, stated once: a **RECEIPT** reports an act that LANDED (the store changed, or a
setting she flipped took effect) — her setting governs it. A **REFUSAL** reports that nothing happened and
says why — P-2 (fire-and-DO) makes it always-show. A **DIRECTION** ("finish the ceremony, then run this
again"; the ⌘Z-at-the-junction hint) reports no act and must reach her, so it rides the refusal class. An
**OFFER** carries a button and always shows. `speak` infers refusal/offer, so **every refusal site in the app
is byte-unchanged** — the diff touches only what I judged a receipt.

**Where the class is decided:** at the DOOR that produced the message, never in the centre and never by a view
reading the words (the `RecoveryStatus` rule, reused rather than re-derived).

#### R-5 · THE BATCH'S OWN CALLS (recorded, not asked — §8's rule)

1. **The four forwarders' shadow kind.** `EditorViewModel`/`BlockTOCViewModel`/`CanvasViewModel`/`CompareBoardModel` deliver their `statusMessage` with `outgoingKind`, named by the writing door and RESET after each delivery. The alternative — converting `statusMessage` into a computed forwarder over a classed value (`TakesViewModel`'s shape) — is the prettier one and would have meant editing ~100 assignment sites across four files for ~15 receipts. The shadow's reset is what makes every untouched site behave identically, and the invariant is pinned wherever a receipt is followed by a refusal.
2. **`spoken` (= `current ?? quietLine`).** Added so the twenty-two shipped pins that assert WHAT was said stay kind-agnostic, and so the pins that assert SILENCE actually mean it. The slot pins read `current`/`quietLine` directly, which keeps the distinction visible.
3. **The `.off` drop leaves the screen alone.** A receipt she asked not to see does not sweep away a refusal she is still reading.
4. **One message at a time across both slots.** A new message clears the other slot, so the centre can never show a stale quiet receipt under a fresh toast. Pinned.
5. **`ReceiptStyleCopy`'s never-leave-out sentence** follows `SavepointCadenceCopy`'s bar: a setting called "Nothing" that did not say refusals still show would be the J8 copy-truth defect.
6. **The Confirmations section is its own**, not a row inside Editor or Writing: it is neither the writing surface's look nor the document's habits.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**[BLOCKER] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Library/NoteDeletion.swift:177` (with `:115`, `:133`, `:156`) ·
Three REFUSAL outcomes of the note-delete door are spoken through `status.receipt(…)`, so her confirmations
setting can hide — and `off` can silence — a refusal. This breaks the letter's own always-show guarantee, P-2,
and the sentence the Settings pane prints to her.**

*Mechanism, traced.* `NoteDeletion.run` returns a bare `String` with no outcome discriminator, and **three** of its
four return paths report that **nothing happened**:

- `:115` `guard !postIDs.isEmpty else { return RecoveryCopy.notesAlreadyGone(0) }`
- `:133` `guard !notes.isEmpty else { return RecoveryCopy.notADeletableNote }` — *"Scraps go one at a time — delete the scraps themselves."*
- `:156` `guard deleted > 0 else { return RecoveryCopy.notesAlreadyGone(postIDs.count) }` — *"That note is already gone."*

`fire` (`:177`) now hands **all four** to `session.status.receipt(…)`. The repo's own doc on the copy says the
opposite, verbatim (`App/Variorum/Shared/RecoveryCopy.swift:725–727`): *"Every named note was already gone (the
double-press / racing-window case). **Nothing happened, so this is a refusal's voice, not a receipt's** — it goes
where `DeletionRefusal`'s sentences go."* The batch's own stated rule agrees (the RECORD: *"a REFUSAL reports that
nothing happened and says why — P-2 makes it always-show"*), as do `StatusCenter.swift:26` (*"ALWAYS the toast,
under every setting"*), `Sources/VariorumCore/Models/Enums.swift:104`, and the user-facing promise the pane prints
at `AppSettingsView.swift:196` / `ReceiptStyleCopy.swift:45`: *"Whichever you choose, **anything Variorum REFUSES
still shows** as a note at the bottom of the window."*

*What she sees.* Under **`.off`**: select notes in the Library, Delete, confirm, and every one of them was already
tombstoned (a second window, the Trash, a pull that landed the tombstones, a stale list) → **nothing is deleted and
nothing is said**; the door reads as dead. Under **`.quiet` — HER DEFAULT** — it is no better: the Library, the
Pool and Archived have **no bottom bar**, so `quietLine` is written and nothing renders it (R-Q23's ruled arm),
and the refusal is invisible there too. Before 18i every one of these toasted.

*Reachability, stated honestly.* `notesAlreadyGone` is reachable today from all four `fire` doors (the racing-window
/ stale-list / already-tombstoned case the copy exists for). `notADeletableNote` is **not** reachable from a shipped
door right now — `CommitBar.swift:715` braces its row on `model.header?.kind == .post` and pools mount
`BlocksAreaView`, never `PostDetailView` — but it is the **belt** behind that brace, and its own pin
(`NoteDeletionDoorsTests.swift:310–324`) records that the brace has already failed once (*"an invariant that was
TRUE when it was written and that item 3 of the same batch silently invalidated by giving four new doors a road to
`deleteContainer`"*). 18i converts that belt from "always speaks" to "speaks only if a bar happens to be mounted and
the setting is not `off`", which is the 13l Act 7 walk defect re-armed.

*Why the green suite missed it.* Both shipped pins on this copy (`NoteDeletionDoorsTests.swift:258`, `:324`;
`SnippetsRefreshTests.swift:184`) call `NoteDeletion.run` **directly** and assert the returned string. Nothing pins
`fire`'s routing, so the misclassification is invisible to every test in the repo.

*Proposed fix.* Give `run` the discriminator the split doors already have — the `SplitAtNewlinesCopy.acted` shape,
one predicate with one home: return `(text: String, isRefusal: Bool)` (or a two-case enum), and have `fire` speak
`status.speak(…)` for the three no-op paths and `status.receipt(…)` only for `movedToTrashReceipt`. **Red-on-old pin
(easy, and it is the pin this whole axis is missing):** with `receiptStyle = .off`, fire the door over an
already-tombstoned post and assert `status.current?.text == RecoveryCopy.notesAlreadyGone(1)` and
`status.current?.kind == .refusal` — red on this tree (`current == nil`, `lastDroppedReceipt` holds the words),
green after. While fixing, **re-audit every `receipt(…)`/`showReceipt(…)` whose argument is a COMPUTED string**
rather than a fixed sentence; that is the whole class, and MINOR-7 below is its second instance.

---

**[MAJOR] · `EditorViewModel.swift:72–95` · `BlockTOCView.swift:89–109` · `CanvasViewModel.swift:83–103` ·
`CompareBoardView.swift:175–195` · F-0: the forwarder rule is COPY-PASTED into four view models — three of them
byte-identically, the fourth already divergent. Two copies of one rule is the drift class the round's own review
focus names; this is four.**

*Mechanism, traced.* The stateful rule (`name the next kind → deliver → RESET to .refusal`) lives in four places.
The three non-Editor copies are literally identical, comment block included:

```swift
guard let statusMessage else { return }
session.status.deliver(statusMessage, kind: outgoingKind)
outgoingKind = .refusal
…
@ObservationIgnored private var outgoingKind: StatusCenter.Kind = .refusal
func showReceipt(_ message: String) { outgoingKind = .receipt; statusMessage = message }
```

`EditorViewModel`'s copy has **already diverged** — it routes through a private `setStatusMessage(_:kind:)`
(`:92–95`) that the other three do not have, and it names its kinds at three doors rather than one. The reset is an
INVARIANT (a missed reset makes the next refusal speak as a receipt, which under `.off` is silence); an invariant
maintained in four hand-written copies is precisely what F-0 forbids, and a fifth forwarder added later will be a
fifth copy.

*What the record's own call #1 answered, and what it did not.* The batch weighed "the shadow" against "convert
`statusMessage` into a computed forwarder over a classed value across ~100 assignment sites" and correctly picked
the shadow. That is not the question F-0 asks. The third option — the one that keeps every one of those ~100 sites
untouched **and** gives the rule one home — was not considered: a small shared value beside the centre, e.g.

```swift
struct StatusForwarder {               // Registry/, beside StatusCenter
    let status: StatusCenter
    var outgoing: StatusCenter.Kind = .refusal
    mutating func deliver(_ text: String?) {
        guard let text else { return }
        status.deliver(text, kind: outgoing)
        outgoing = .refusal
    }
}
```

Each model then carries `@ObservationIgnored private var forwarder: StatusForwarder`, its `didSet` is one line
(`forwarder.deliver(statusMessage)`), and `showReceipt` is `forwarder.outgoing = .receipt; statusMessage = message`.
~20 lines net, zero call-site edits, one home for the reset. **No test pin is owed** (architectural finding, per the
hallucination guard) — but the traced degradation is the one above, and the drift is already measurable in the
fourth copy.

*Separately, and this is the clean half:* I checked every road the shadow can take and found **no leak**. `didSet`
in Swift fires on every set with no equality gate; the only way to strand `outgoingKind = .receipt` is to follow it
with a `nil` assignment, and every one of the four `showReceipt`/`setStatusMessage` doors takes a non-optional
`String`. The self-clearing `hintClearTask` writes `statusMessage = nil` only *after* a delivery has already reset
the shadow. **J25's specific worry is closed** — see the clean bill.

**[MINOR] · `Core/Views/QuietReceiptLine.swift:17–22, :54` + `CommitBar.swift:339` · The idle slot is weightless
only on the HORIZONTAL axis. In the one composition whose axis is vertical — the book's sidebar note-box footer —
it permanently reserves a blank line, and the oracle that is supposed to pin "no room when there is nothing to say"
asserts WIDTH only.**

*Measured* (throwaway `NSHostingView` probe reproducing the view's exact modifier chain, run once, deleted):
`Text("")` with `.lineLimit(2).fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)` measures **width 0, height 14 pt**.
Composed into `boxFooter`'s `VStack(spacing: 4)`, the footer's idle fitting height equals its speaking height
(**37 pt both**) — i.e. the footer is permanently **18 pt taller** than before 18i and carries an empty row between
the divider and the counts whenever nothing is being said. The view's own doc claims the opposite in general terms
(*"zero width, nothing drawn, no reflow"*), which is true for the three flat-bar sites and false for this one; and
`ConfirmationsSettingTests.swift:195–205` pins `fittingSize.width == 0` three times and never the height, so the
reservation is unpinned in both directions.

*Proposed fix (either is fine, but the doc must match).* Keep the reservation and say so — add
`#expect(host.fittingSize.height …)` to the oracle and correct the header to "zero width; one line's height in the
vertical composition, reserved deliberately so the counts and `?` never move" — or collapse it in the box only
(`.frame(height: item == nil ? 0 : nil)`), accepting an 18 pt shift of the counts row when a receipt lands. No
red-on-old pin is owed for the doc half; the height assertion is the pin for whichever behaviour is chosen.

#### NITs

  `acted` computes `results.contains { !$0.isNoOp }`: one rule, two spellings, six lines apart. `guard acted(results)
  else { return whenNothingSplit }` collapses them.
- **`WriteTakesPanel.swift:104–107`** — under `.off`, the Write fan panel still renders the board's receipt in its
  own slot, so "off" is not off on that one surface. Defensible (it is a scoped local slot, like the Library's
  caption, and the RECORD lists that class as out of scope) — recorded so the next reader does not read it as a bug.

  `lineLimit` half of the b6dae25 rule is honoured; selection is a small extra hit-target in a bar full of doors.

**[BLOCKER] `NoteDeletion` — three refusals on the receipt road — AGREE. Fully, and it is the right
severity.**

Traced, not accepted on the reading: `NoteDeletion.run` (`Features/Library/NoteDeletion.swift:114–158`)
returns a bare `String`, and three of its four returns report that nothing happened —
`:115` (`notesAlreadyGone(0)`, the empty gesture), `:133` (`notADeletableNote`, the Act-7 kind fence),
`:156` (`notesAlreadyGone(postIDs.count)`, the race where every named note was already tombstoned) —
while `:157` alone is the real receipt. `fire` (`:177`) hands **all four** to `session.status.receipt(…)`,
which `StatusCenter.slot(for:)` (`:187–198`) routes by `receiptStyle`: `.quiet` → `quietLine`, `.off` →
dropped. The copy's own doc says the opposite in words I did not write and should have read at
classification time — `Shared/RecoveryCopy.swift:726`: *"Nothing happened, so this is a refusal's voice,
not a receipt's — it goes where `DeletionRefusal`'s sentences go."* My own RECORD states the same rule
two paragraphs above the table that then breaks it. That is the finding, and it is mine.

**Where it bites, verified:** none of the four `fire` doors mounts a bottom bar. `QuietReceiptLine` is
composed at exactly six sites, all of them Write's `CommitBar` (three tiers + the sidebar box's footer),
`TakesBottomBar` (two arrangements) — grep-verified; the mounts are `EditorView.swift:132`,
`RootView.swift:605`, `TakesBoardView.swift:174`, `LensesBoardView.swift:146`. The Library
(`LibraryCatalogView:277`), the Pool (`PoolPostsView:215`) and Archived (`ArchivedView:101`) have **no
bar at all**, so under HER DEFAULT the refusal is written to `quietLine` and rendered by nobody (R-Q23's
ruled arm), and under `.off` it is dropped outright. Before 18i all three toasted. Row 42 of my table
("the deletion report") treated a four-outcome door as if it had one outcome; that is the exact
classification error, and the reviewer's reading of it is correct.

**Reachability:** `notesAlreadyGone` is live today (double-press, a second window, a stale list, a pull
that landed the tombstones). `notADeletableNote` is the belt behind `CommitBar.swift:722`'s
`model.header?.kind == .post` brace, and `NoteDeletionDoorsTests.swift:310–324` records in its own doc
that this brace has already been silently invalidated once. Converting a belt from "always speaks" to
"speaks only where a bar happens to be mounted, and only if the setting is not `off`" is not a belt.

**The fix I would make** — the `SplitAtNewlinesCopy.acted` shape, one predicate with one home, **and the
3C parity pattern so not one shipped pin is edited**:

- a small value `NoteDeletion.Report { let text: String; let isRefusal: Bool }`, produced by a new
  `report(session:postIDs:)` that holds today's body — the three no-op returns carry `isRefusal: true`,
  `movedToTrashReceipt` carries `false`;
- **`run(session:postIDs:)` stays byte-identical in name and return type**, forwarding
  (`try await report(…).text`), so `NoteDeletionDoorsTests` (6 call sites), `SnippetsRefreshTests:184`
  and `LibraryViewModel.delete` compile and pass UNMODIFIED — zero test edits is the parity proof;
- `fire` routes: `outcome.isRefusal ? status.speak(outcome.text) : status.receipt(outcome.text)`.

**Recommended, and the orchestrator's to arbitrate** (it is a shape question, not a product one): put
that ternary in ONE place rather than at each door — `SpokenOutcome { text; isRefusal }` beside the
centre plus `StatusCenter.say(_:)` — because the audit below found a SECOND door that needs the same
two lines, and `runStructural`'s `StructuralOutcome.noteIsRefusal` (`EditorSurfaceController.swift:1746`,
routed at `:2757`) is already the same rule one layer over. Three spellings of "did this door act?" is
the drift class F-0 names. The minimum honest fix is the per-door discriminator; the shared value is the
one I would build.

**Red-on-old pin** (the axis the whole batch was missing — new, in `ConfirmationsSettingTests`):
`aDeleteThatDeletedNothingStillSpeaks` — seed a post, tombstone it directly through `ops`, set
`receiptStyle = .off`, call `NoteDeletion.fire(session:postIDs:[dead])`, poll the bounded async way
(`fire` is a detached `Task`; the repo's poll rule, never a RunLoop pump) until
`status.current != nil || status.lastDroppedReceipt != nil`, then
`#expect(status.current?.text == RecoveryCopy.notesAlreadyGone(1))` and
`#expect(status.current?.kind == .refusal)` and `#expect(status.lastDroppedReceipt == nil)`.
**Red on this tree**: `current == nil`, the words sitting in `lastDroppedReceipt`. A second arm pins the
belt: `fire` over a POOL id under `.quiet` → `current?.text == RecoveryCopy.notADeletableNote`, kind
`.refusal`, `quietLine == nil`.

**[MAJOR] The forwarder rule copied into four view models (F-0) — AGREE, and the reviewer's
`StatusForwarder` shape is right.**

The four copies are real and I counted them again myself: `EditorViewModel.swift:80–95`,
`BlockTOCView.swift:87–109`, `CanvasViewModel.swift:81–103`, `CompareBoardView.swift:173–195` —
`outgoingKind` appears at 20 lines across the four files, three of them byte-identical including the
comment block. My RECORD's call #1 weighed the shadow against converting `statusMessage` into a classed
value across ~100 assignment sites and picked the shadow; the reviewer is right that the third option —
**one home for the rule AND zero call-site edits** — was never on my list, and it is strictly better than
what I built. The degradation is not hypothetical: the fourth copy has already diverged (`EditorViewModel`
alone routes through `setStatusMessage(_:kind:)` at `:92` and names kinds at three doors), and the reset
is an INVARIANT — a missed reset makes the next refusal speak as a receipt, which under `.off` is
silence. That is the BLOCKER's failure mode arriving by drift instead of by classification.

**Where it lives and what it costs.** I would put it in `Registry/StatusCenter.swift` itself rather than a
new file — twenty lines whose only reason to exist is that seam's rule belong beside the seam, and a
`StatusForwarder.swift` holding one struct is a file that will be read as a subsystem. `@MainActor`
(it calls a `@MainActor` method), `struct` not `class` (the reset is value semantics; each model owns
one). Each model then carries `@ObservationIgnored private var forwarder: StatusForwarder`, initialised
in its init after `session` is assigned (four inits touched, mechanical), its `didSet` becomes the one
line `forwarder.deliver(statusMessage)`, and `showReceipt` becomes
`forwarder.outgoing = .receipt; statusMessage = message`. `EditorViewModel`'s `setStatusMessage(_:kind:)`
survives as `forwarder.outgoing = kind; statusMessage = message` — the divergence becomes a parameter
instead of a second copy. Net ≈ −25 lines across four files, **zero call-site edits**, and the ~100 bare
`statusMessage = …` assignments stay byte-unchanged, which was the whole point of the shadow.

No test pin is owed (architectural, per the guard) and I am not inventing one; the existing kind pins
(`ConfirmationsSettingTests`, `StatusCenterTests`) cover the behaviour through all four models unchanged,
which is the right proof for a refactor of this kind.

**On the clean half — I agree and re-derived it.** The shadow cannot strand: `didSet` fires on every set
with no equality gate; all four doors that raise it (`showReceipt` ×3, `setStatusMessage`/`showTransient`)
take a non-optional `String` (`EditorViewModel.swift:92`, `:2455–2476`, `:3433–3444`); the only

already reset it. J25's worry is closed.

**[MINOR-1] The idle slot is weightless only horizontally; the box footer reserves a blank line; the
oracle pins width only — AGREE, and I MEASURED it myself rather than taking the number.**

Throwaway `swiftc`/`NSHostingView` probe in the scratchpad (outside the repo, reproducing the exact
modifier chain and `boxFooter`'s `VStack(spacing: 4)`): the idle line is **width 0, height 14** at both
`lines: 1` and `lines: 2`; the footer's fitting height is **37 idle and 37 speaking** — identical, i.e.
the blank row (14 + 4) is permanently reserved. The view's header claims "zero width, nothing drawn, no
reflow", which is true of the three flat-bar sites and false of the box; and
`ConfirmationsSettingTests.swift:195–205` asserts `fittingSize.width == 0` three times and the height
never, so the reservation is unpinned in both directions. Both halves of the finding hold.

**Which road, and why: (a) — keep the reservation, pin it, correct the doc.** Not (b). The box's footer
carries the counts AND the `?` helper door; collapsing the slot would move a DOOR 18 pt when a receipt
lands and 18 pt back six seconds later, under her cursor — which is the precise hazard `QuietReceiptLine`
is always-mounted to avoid (its own doc says so), and the walk's capture 10 shows her the geometry as
built. The cost of (a) is one blank row inside a box whose content already scrolls in a column-fixed
frame; the cost of (b) is a moving door. So: correct the header to say what is true — *zero WIDTH in the
flat bars; one line's height in the vertical composition, reserved deliberately so the counts and the `?`
never move* — and make the oracle say it too.

**The height oracle** (extending `theQuietSlotIsWeightlessUntilItSpeaks`, not a new suite): mount a
SECOND host with `lines: 2` (the composition the current oracle never measures), and assert idle
`fittingSize.height > 0` **and** `idleHeight == speakingHeight` — the stability claim, in both directions,
so a future collapse of the slot goes red at the pin rather than in her hands. The `lines: 1` host keeps
its three width assertions unchanged. No red-on-old is owed (doc/pin finding); the height assertion IS
the pin for the behaviour chosen.

**[MINOR-6] Delete-in-Every-Take has no `edits.isEmpty` guard — DISPUTE. The stated mechanism is
unreachable, and the pin the finding proposes would be GREEN ON BOTH SIDES.**

The finding says *"when every take skips ('no unique match'), `applied == 0`"*. Traced at
`EditorSurfaceController.swift:2446–2481`: the per-target loop's FIRST branch is
`if take.id == target.renderedID`, which appends an edit built from `target.intraRange` **without any
match test at all** and does `applied += 1` before `continue`. The rendered take never takes the
`uniqueRange` road — that road exists only for the OTHER takes. And `targets` is non-empty by construction
(`guard let first = touched.first` at `:2402`, one target per touched entry). So on every road a user can
drive, `applied ≥ targets.count ≥ 1`, and *"Deleted in 0 takes."* cannot be produced.

That is exactly why the Replace twin's guard exists and this one's does not: in
`replaceInEveryTake` the rendered take's edit is itself conditional — `guard !matches.isEmpty else
{ continue }` (`:2611`) — because a match can MOVE under the deferred find window, so `edits` there really
can end up empty. The two doors are not symmetric, and the asymmetry is the substrate's, not an omission.

**The only residue**, stated honestly so it is not rediscovered: if the rendered take were concurrently
archived or tombstoned by another window between the surface's index and the fan read (the
`status == .active` filter at `:2450` would then exclude it) AND no other take had a unique match, `edits`
would be empty, `editTakesAtomically([])` returns 0 without throwing
(`Operations+TakeEdits.swift:50`), `landed` is true, and "Deleted in 0 takes." would speak. Reaching that
in a pin means deliberately desynchronising the editor's own projection from the store — i.e. pinning a
corrupted surface, not a door. I do not think that is a pin worth having, and I will not write one to
make a finding true.

**If the orchestrator wants the guard anyway** (the twin's one line, speaking `FindReplaceGate`-shaped
copy), I will add it and record it as **defensive symmetry, not a fix** — with no pin, because there is no
red-on-old to have. My recommendation is to record the trace instead: it belongs in the audit below as a
verdict, which is where I have put it.

*(Every `status.receipt(…)` / `showReceipt(…)` / `showTransientReceipt(…)` / `setStatus(…)` call in the
app, filtered to those whose argument is computed rather than a fixed sentence. The question asked of each:
**can it ever report a no-op?** Sites whose argument is a fixed constant — `"Committed."`,
`"Blocks joined — ⌥⌘Z undoes it."`, `QuickNoteCopy.filedNote`, `BlockSelectionCopy.archivedNote`, the two
`"type away."` lines — are omitted: a fixed sentence cannot lie about a count it does not carry, and each
is already inside a `landed` / `do` success path.)*

| Site | Computed from | Can it report a no-op? |
|---|---|---|
| `NoteDeletion.swift:177` | `run`'s four outcomes | **YES ×3 — THE BLOCKER.** `:115`, `:133`, `:156` |
| **`ShellActions.swift:238`** (import) | `importer.lastReport` | **YES — A SECOND INSTANCE, reachable in one gesture.** Import an EMPTY (or whitespace-only) `.md`: `readFiles` reads it, `ops.importPost` throws `emptyImport` (`Operations+Import.swift:63`), the compound's inner `catch` collects it as a SKIP, `imported == 0`, `lastError` is explicitly set nil (`ImportModel.swift:91`), and `report` (`:239–253`) yields *"Skipped: x.md (nothing to import)."* — spoken through `status.receipt`. #### Findings, severity-ranked

**[BLOCKER] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Takes/TakesViewModel.swift:966` · `:1128` · `:1466` · `:1572`
· `:2346` · `:2361` · `:2376` · `:2398` · EIGHT board messages that report that NOTHING happened are classed
`RecoveryStatus.receipt`, and 18i's one load-bearing move — letting that class RIDE to the shell
(`:143–154`) — turns every one of them into a setting-governed receipt. Under `.off` they say nothing at
all; under `.quiet` they land in the muted bar line instead of the toast the Settings pane promises. This is
round 1's BLOCKER again, in a second and larger family, and it is exactly the family the RECORD's table
declared safe without auditing.**

*Mechanism, traced.* `TakesViewModel.status`'s `didSet` was `session.status.speak(status.text)` before this
letter — ALWAYS the toast. The letter changed it to
`session.status.deliver(status.text, kind: status.isRefusal ? .refusal : .receipt)` (the diff at `:143–154`),
so the board's own `RecoveryStatus` now decides *visibility*, not only the panel's colour. `RecoveryStatus`
states its own contract at `App/Variorum/Shared/RecoveryCopy.swift:848–851`: *"`case receipt` — Something
happened, and this says what… `case refusal` — Nothing happened, and this says why."* Eight assignments
break it:

- `:1572` `commitFocusedTake()` with no focused pane → `.receipt("Click into a take first — ⌘S commits the take you're in.")`
- `:2346` `stepTakes(by:)` with no focused pane → `.receipt("Click into a take first — ⌃⌘← and ⌃⌘→ step through its siblings.")`
- `:2361` `stepTakes(by:)` on a one-take block → `.receipt("This block has one take — ⌘T branches a second.")`
- `:2376` `chooseFocusedTake()` with no focused pane → `.receipt("Click into a take first — ⌘⏎ chooses the take you're in.")`
- `:2398` `archiveFocusedTake()` with no focused pane → `.receipt("Click into a take first — ⌘⇧A archives the take you're in.")`
- `:966` `pick(columnID:…)` on the MAIN column → `.receipt("The main column shows the note's chosen takes — use ✓ to change them.")`
- `:1128` `adoptColumn(_:)` on the MAIN column → `.receipt("This column IS the note — nothing to adopt.")`
- `:1466` the lens fallback's `.gone`/`.foreign` arm → `.receipt(LensFallbackCopy.nothingToRestore)`

Every one returns early or falls through without a write. `StatusCenter.slot(for:)` (`:209–220`) then routes
`.receipt` by `receiptStyle`: `.quiet` → `quietLine`, `.off` → **nil, dropped**.

*What she sees.* All eight are live doors: `commitFocusedTake` / `chooseFocusedTake` / `archiveFocusedTake` /
`stepTakes` are registered command handlers on `TakesBoardView.swift:269/:381/:383/:385/:387` and
`LensesBoardView.swift:203/:320/:322/:324/:326`, and `pick`/`adoptColumn` are one click each in Lenses.
Neither board renders a local status slot — both carry the comment *"13b 1b (AD-14): the transient status
line moved to the ONE StatusCenter"* (`TakesBoardView.swift:149`, `LensesBoardView.swift:134`) — so **under
`.off`, ⌘S in Takes with no take focused is completely silent**, as are ⌘⏎, ⌘⇧A, ⌃⌘←/→ and Adopt on the main
column. Under **`.quiet` — her default** — they appear as a truncated muted line at the bar's trailing end,
which is not what `ReceiptStyleCopy.alwaysShownNote` prints to her at `AppSettingsView.swift:196`:
*"Whichever you choose, anything Variorum REFUSES still shows as a note at the bottom of the window — a door
that can't act always says why."* Before 18i all eight were toast cards under every condition.

*Why the audit missed it, precisely.* The RECORD's table row 18 rules the whole family in one line —
*"`TakesViewModel.status` forward (`:146`) · every board message · **CLASSED ALREADY** · the board decided it
at the door since the post-13l polish round; 18i just lets the class RIDE"* — and round 1's sweep checked
*"every `setStatus(` caller on the board… all 13"*. But `setStatus` is only one of the doors into `status`:
there are **25 direct `status = .receipt(…)` assignments inside `TakesViewModel` itself**, and they were
never enumerated by either agent. The mis-classification is pre-13i (post-13l); what 18i did is make it
*decide whether she sees the message at all*, which is this letter's to own — the identical reasoning J29
was confirmed on.

*Why no test caught it.* Nothing pins the KIND of a board refusal. `NoteVersionsPaneTests.theBoardTellsAReceiptFromARefusal`
drives `setStatus`/`speak` directly (the mechanism), and `TakeStructureDoorTests` asserts the WORDS, which are
identical on both roads — the same blind axis J32 was raised for.

*Proposed fix.* One word at each of the eight sites: `.receipt(` → `.refusal(` (or route them through the
model's own `speak(_:)`, which is `setRefusal`, `:1674–1676`). Note the deliberate consequence, so it is not
a surprise: `WriteTakesPanel.swift:107` paints `status.isRefusal ? tokens.alarm : tokens.muted`, so these
eight will read in the alarm token there — which is exactly what their siblings in
`TakesStructureController` (*"Click into a block first…"*, table row 21) already do through `speak`, so the
fix makes the panel consistent rather than introducing a new look. **Red-on-old pin** (in
`ConfirmationsSettingTests` beside J29's, or in `TakeStructureDoorTests` which already owns the board
harness): with `receiptStyle = .off`, call `model.commitFocusedTake()` on a board with no focused pane and
assert `session.status.current?.text == "Click into a take first — ⌘S commits the take you're in."`,
`current?.kind == .refusal`, `lastDroppedReceipt == nil` — **red on this tree** (`current == nil`, the words
sitting in `lastDroppedReceipt`). A second arm on `adoptColumn` over the main column covers the click road.

*One milder sibling on the same slot, for the same pass* (the row-35 / J37 class, not the refusal class):
`:1202–1210` `writeNewTakesEverywhere()` speaks `.receipt("New takes written on \(picks.count) block(s) — …")`
and `Operations.branchAllFans(post:)` (`Sources/VariorumCore/Operations/Operations+Versions.swift:481–487`)
returns `[:]` without throwing on a post with no renderable slots — so *"New takes written on 0 blocks"* is
producible while nothing was written. Same one-line predicate as the import's and the export's.

**[MAJOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Core/Views/QuietReceiptLine.swift:24–39` + `App/Variorum/VariorumTests/ConfirmationsSettingTests.swift:364–414`
(J31) · The fix's central claim — *"the counts and the `?` door never move"* — is FALSE in the one
composition the road was chosen for, and the height oracle that was supposed to prove it cannot fail. Both
agents' "37 pt idle AND 37 pt speaking" was measured at a width the box never has.**

*Mechanism, measured* (two throwaway `swiftc`/`NSHostingView` probes, scratchpad, outside the repo):

1. **`NSHostingView.fittingSize` is the UNCONSTRAINED ideal size — the host's frame does not constrain it.**
   The view's exact modifier chain with `lines: 2` in a host framed at 200×40 reports, for a 125-character
   receipt, `fittingSize = 896.0 × 14.0` — one line, at 896 pt of width. So `boxHost.frame = NSRect(… width: 200 …)`
   at `ConfirmationsSettingTests.swift:368` buys the oracle nothing: `boxHost.fittingSize.height == idleBoxHeight`
   (`:404–405`, `:414`) is true for **every** string and **every** `lines` value. The stability half of the
   new pin cannot bite. (Its `idleBoxHeight > 0` half is honest and does bite — that is the half the
   collapse-road probe saw fail.)
2. **Constrained to the box's real column it is not stable.** Mounting the footer's actual shape —
   `VStack(spacing: 4) { Divider(); QuietReceiptLine(lines: 2); HStack { counts; Spacer; ? } }` inside
   `.frame(width: 200)`, i.e. `CommitBar.swift:331–348` — measures **37 pt idle → 51 pt speaking**. Not only
   for a long sentence: it is 51 pt for the pin's OWN example, *"Blocks joined — ⌥⌘Z undoes it."* (30
   characters at `tokens.small` = 11.5 pt monospaced ≈ 207 pt > 200), which wraps to the second line
   `.lineLimit(2)` allows. Remove the width constraint and the same probe reports 37 → 37, which is the
   number the round-1 finding, the implementer's re-measurement and J31's disposition all rest on.

*What this means, stated honestly.* The behaviour is **not a regression** — road (a) as built moves the
counts row and the `?` door by **one** line (14 pt) where the rejected road (b) would have moved them by
two (28 pt), so keeping the reservation still halves the noise. What is wrong is (i) the header's absolute
claim at `:31–38` (*"collapsing the row would move a door 18 pt… the reserved row costs a blank line and
nothing below it moves"*) — the door moves anyway for any receipt over ~28 characters at that column width,
which is most of them; and (ii) a pin presented in the record as *"idle == speaking in BOTH"* that is
structurally incapable of failing on the axis it names. The disposition chose road (a) over road (b) on
exactly the premise this falsifies.

*Proposed fix (the pin first — there is a real red).* Make the oracle measure the composition it names:
constrain the width (wrap the rootView in `.frame(width: 200)`, or set `boxHost`'s `sizingOptions` /
`widthAnchor` before reading `fittingSize`) — **red on this tree at 37 vs 51**. Then either (a) keep the
one-line reservation and correct the header to what is true — *the row grows by at most one line when a
receipt wraps, and nothing OUTSIDE the box moves because `SidebarNoteBox` is framed by the column
(`SidebarNoteBox.swift:18–27`) and this bar sits inside its `ScrollView`* — or (b) reserve the full two
lines (`.frame(height: twoLines, alignment: .topLeading)` in the `lines > 1` composition) so the claim
becomes literally true. Either is cheap; the width-constrained assertion is the pin for whichever is chosen.

**[BLOCKER · J38] Eight `TakesViewModel` refusals classed `.receipt` — AGREE, and the reviewer's reading of

Traced at all eight: `:966` `pick` on the main column (the `switch`'s `.main` arm sets the line and the

happened, and this says why"*). Before this letter the board's `status` didSet was

`deliver(status.text, kind: status.isRefusal ? .refusal : .receipt)` (`TakesViewModel.swift:143–154`), which

I checked the blast radius myself: all eight are live doors (`TakesBoardView.swift:269/:381–387`,
`LensesBoardView.swift:203/:320–326` register the four commands; `pick`/`adoptColumn` are one click each in

#### R-6 · WHICH TOKENS A PALETTE OWNS (the derivation table — the brief's ask)

**The rule I decided by**, stated once: a palette owns the slots her ruling NAMES — *"the room (the tan
panels), the wash, the accent (the coloured chrome words), the take tint/line and the hairline"* — plus,
in DARK ONLY, the two that carry the room's job when the room is black (R51). Every other slot is what
makes a voice a voice, and moving one would make a palette a third voice, which R1/R12 forbid. The list
lives in the type itself: the eight owned slots are `var` on `VoiceTokens` and `applying(_:)` is their one
writer; everything else is `let`.

| Slot | Light | Dark | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `room` | **DERIVED** | **BLACK** | her "tan panels". R51 falls out of the table (dark lightness 0), never a special case |
| `wash` | **DERIVED** | **DERIVED** | selected rows + the changing-block wash — she sees it on every row she clicks |
| `accent` | **DERIVED** | **DERIVED** | *"the lightly colored text like (this note) and commit"* — the ask's second half |
| `takeTint` · `takeLine` | **DERIVED** | **DERIVED** | the ruling names the take tints |
| `line` | **DERIVED** | **DERIVED** | the hairline the ruling names |
| `surface` · `card` | the VOICE's | **DERIVED** | light: the mockup keeps every card's page the voice's paper — paper is paper. Dark: the room is black, so the paper carries the whisper of hue instead (the mockup's own dark preview) |
| `ink` · `muted` · `faint` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | prose and quiet chrome are the voice's register; recolouring them is a voice change (13s's) |
| `chosen` · `positive` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | "✓ chosen" is a MEANING, not a decoration — it must mean the same thing under every palette |
| `ring` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | the editing indicator is a state mark (R14/R22), and U-7 ties it to her preference, not to colour taste |
| `star` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | her direct call, pre-13u Act 10 item 13: *"i like the blue star"* — blue in every voice, so in every palette |
| `alarm` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | a refusal must read as a refusal; a palette that could tint the alarm toward its own accent would undo the post-13l ledger row 29 fix |
| `commentTint` · `commentInk` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | R7's comment register is its own language beside the prose |
| `codeTint` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | 13k K10 chose it *neutral to the voice's room on purpose*; a palette hue would make it a callout |
| `seam` | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | the dotted seam is the boundary MECHANISM (R6), not a hairline — the ruling names `line`, and these are different jobs |
| every type + idiom slot | the VOICE's | the VOICE's | R1/R12: this is the whole reason a palette is not a third voice |

**The two intensity tables, and where the numbers come from.** All 32 mockup cards were read as HSL; the
tables were fitted to them. **All eleven two-tone and bold rooms and ten of the eleven washes are
reproduced BYTE-EXACT from their seed pairs alone** (teal & rust's wash is one value off in one channel —
mockup `C2EAE6`, shipped `C3EAE6` — rounding), **and the nine accents that already cleared AA are
byte-exact too** *(the sentence corrected at the ladder, R1-5: it had said "every … BYTE-EXACT")* — that is
what proved the mockup was one rule with two levels rather than 32 hand-picked cards, and it is pinned for
two of them (`theTablesReproduceTheApprovedMockupsRoomAndWash`). The four PASTEL cards were drawn a hair
lighter than the two-tone ones (room L .965 vs .955, accent L .420 vs .400); they collapse into the soft
table here — within seven values out of 255 (lavender's accent `5230A6` → `4E2D9F` is the widest; *"2–3"*
was the record's understatement, corrected at R1-5), recorded rather than given a third table.

| Token | soft L (light / dark) | soft S≤ | bold L (light / dark) | bold S≤ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| room | .955 / .000 | .55 | .920 / .000 | .75 |
| surface | — / .070 | .32 | — / .080 | .42 |
| card | — / .105 | .32 | — / .115 | .42 |
| wash | .890 / .150 | .56 | .841 / .170 | .70 |
| accent | .400 / .680 | .70 | .420 / .660 | .90 |
| takeTint | .949 / .060 | .48 | .929 / .070 | .60 |
| takeLine | .840 / .190 | .45 | .780 / .200 | .55 |
| line | .880 / .145 | .35 | .841 / .155 | .50 |

**THE ONE CORRECTION ON TOP, and why it is not a fudge.** HSL lightness is not luminance: a gold at .40 is
nearly twice as bright as a blue at .40. Measured against **the mockup's own cards**, six of the fifteen
accents came out below WCAG AA on their own room — mint 3.51 · gold & black 3.20 · slate & amber 3.42 ·
grey & green 3.25 · cobalt & tangerine 3.52 · **rose & moss 2.56** — while the other nine sat above 5:1.
Lowering the table's number for everyone would have darkened the nine that were already right. So the rule
**steps the accent away from its backdrops until it clears 4.5:1** (darker in light, lighter in dark),
measured against the room AND the wash. It is still ONE rule with no per-preset constant — and it is what
makes **her own hex** safe: `#FFFF00` typed into the custom field produces an accent that reads (pinned,
eleven hostile seeds). **Six preset accents therefore ship DEEPER than the mockup she approved**, named
here so she can say otherwise in one constant edit:

| Preset | the mockup's accent | shipped | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| mint | `#3C9A6F` | **`#2E7555`** | 3.51 → 5.15 on its room |
| gold & black | `#A98523` | **`#81661A`** | 3.20 → 5.05 |
| slate & amber | `#AD791F` | **`#845D17`** | 3.42 → 5.31 |
| grey & green | `#339960` | **`#257147`** | 3.25 → 5.40 |
| cobalt & tangerine | `#CB520C` | **`#933B08`** | 3.52 → 5.82 |
| rose & moss | `#659C3B` | **`#3C5D23`** | 2.56 → 5.85 |

The other nine are the mockup's accents byte-exact. **The full finals table** (all 15 × both appearances ×
room/wash/accent) is pinned as `PaletteDerivationTests.theShippedFamiliesAreTheRecordedOnes` — that pin IS
the record, so a future seed or tone edit shows up as an exact diff instead of a colour nobody noticed
moving. Worst measured ratio across all 15 × 2 appearances × 3 backdrops: **4.50**.
